sd_thin_fin.blurb: Thin Fin is a small granite formation on Moonlight Ridge, in the Needles country of Custer State Park. It has twelve routes, mostly trad with a few bolted lines and a couple of top-rope options. Difficulty is friendly for the Needles: the bulk of the climbs sit between 5.6 and 5.8, with a handful at 5.9 and 5.10. The ridge is a welcome change from the famously run-out face climbing found elsewhere in the Needles, with shorter, better-protected pitches. It is the first formation you meet when coming up from below, so it works as a warm-up stop before moving on to neighbouring formations on the ridge.
sd_thin_fin.parking_note: Leave the car at the Needle's Eye pullout area on the Needles Highway, reached by driving from the Sylvan Lake end, or at one of the small pullouts just before it.
sd_thin_fin.approach: A climbers' trail leaves from the northwest corner of the Needle's Eye lot and heads uphill. Thin Fin is the first formation reached, just before a neighbouring formation called The Galaxy.

sd_wishing_well.blurb: Wishing Well is a compact quartzite pit within the Dells of the Sioux, the gorge just south of Dell Rapids. Eleven of its twelve routes are bolted, with a single trad line, and routes are described as lying on either the north or south side of the pit. Grades cluster around 5.8 and 5.9, with one easier route and one 5.10, so it suits climbers building up on the sport grades. Much of the pit stays shaded through the day, which helps on hot afternoons, but the stone can stay slick for a day after rain. Routes are short, and the setup is tidy for a quick session.

sd_terminator_amphitheatre.blurb: Terminator Amphitheatre is a high alcove on the east side of Spearfish Canyon, in the limestone of the northern Black Hills. It is mostly a winter objective: a freestanding ice pillar draws the attention, rated WI4, and the rock around it carries mixed lines, from moderate up to hard modern grades. One bolted line sits alongside them. Eleven routes are recorded in all. The pillar can be spotted from the canyon road, but reaching it takes a steep bushwhack up a side drainage, so expect a real effort on the way in. It is a place for experienced ice and mixed climbers rather than a casual day out.

sd_south_canyon_wall.blurb: South Canyon Wall is the quiet side of Falling Rock Canyon, a short drive from Rapid City. The cliff is limestone, with steep, bolted faces broken by small pockets. Ten of its eleven routes are sport, with one trad line. Grades start at 5.8 and run through a solid block of 5.9 and 5.10 climbs, finishing with a few at 5.11 and one 5.12. Because it faces north it stays shaded, which makes it an option for afternoons when the other canyon wall is baking. Fewer people come here, and the routes are harder to spot from the rim than on the busier wall across the canyon.
